- TLS versions supported for in-transit (minimum/ideal) and whether mutual TLS is used for internal service-to-service traffic.
- At-rest encryption algorithm and mode (e.g., AES-256-GCM), and whether disk-level or application-level encryption is used for hosted vs private deployments.
- KMS/HSM details: who holds the root key (Redwood vs customer BYOK), HSM vendor (if used), whether keys are marked non-exportable, and FIPS level.
- Rotation cadence for KEKs and DEKs, whether rotation is automatic or requires coordination, and if rotation ever causes downtime.
- Audit logs / access logs for key operations: retention window and a sample log snippet showing timestamp, operator, action.

If you can point us to an example artifact (diagram, rotation policy, or a short log sample) that would be ideal. We are aiming to have final SIG responses by July 29 to keep the contract on track.

Ben — attaching the initial artifacts for your review. See attachments: redwood_kms_rotation_policy.pdf, encryption-dataflow.svg, hsm_access_log_sample.txt, kms_rotation_schedule.csv.

Executive summary (short):
- In transit: We require TLS1.2+ for public endpoints; internal service-to-service uses TLS1.3 by default with mutual TLS available for Dedicated/Private deployments. We support a minimum of TLS1.2 for backwards compatibility; TLS1.3 preferred for hosted endpoints.
- At rest: All customer data is encrypted at rest with AES-256-GCM. For hosted inference, we use envelope encryption: data encrypted with a DEK (AES-256-GCM), DEKs are wrapped by a KEK stored in a KMS or HSM depending on deployment. For Private/VPC and on-prem, customers may furnish BYOKs; we support both cloud KMS and dedicated HSMs.
- KMS/HSM ownership: By default (hosted), Redwood manages KEKs inside an HSM-backed KMS (hardware-backed keys in FIPS 140-2 validated modules). For Dedicated/Private, customers may supply BYOKs. Where BYOK is used, Redwood never has exportable access to the customer's private key material.
- HSM vendor / compliance: We use vetted HSM providers (e.g., Thales/Luna, AWS CloudHSM) for root key custody in hosted setups; modules are validated to FIPS 140-2 Level 3 where available.
- Rotation cadence: DEKs rotate automatically per workload policies (configurable; default 30 days for short-lived DEKs). KEKs/ wrapping keys: default scheduled rewrap every 90 days; emergency/manual rotation process is documented in the attached policy. Rotation is implemented as online rewraps and does not require service downtime in normal operations.
- Audit logs: KMS API calls, HSM admin operations, and key-usage events are logged. Retention: KMS audit logs retained for 2 years; HSM admin logs retained 1 year by default (retention can be extended for Dedicated/Private). Logs contain ISO timestamps, principal identifier (service account or admin), operation, key id, and originating IP. Example lines included in hsm_access_log_sample.txt.

Attached artifacts are redacted where necessary (no customer PII). If you need signed attestations or a more formal evidence bundle (e.g., for SOC 2), let us know and we can coordinate a secure transfer.

Best,

Hi Ben — quick answers inline and a tiny sample pasted below. Also attaching a separate text file with additional log lines for your auditors (sample-hsm-log-lines.txt).

- Sample HSM log lines (redacted):
  2028-07-15T16:08:43Z | admin:ks-agent | OP=KEY_WRAP | key_id=kek-9f4a | result=SUCCESS | src_ip=10.2.34.12
  2028-07-15T16:10:02Z | svc:wrap-worker | OP=UNWRAP | key_id=kek-9f4a | result=SUCCESS | src_ip=10.2.34.55
  2028-07-15T16:11:07Z | admin:rotation-job | OP=KEY_ROLL | key_id=kek-9f4a | result=SUCCESS | note=auto-rotate

- Downtime impact: rotation is implemented as an online key rewrap. We perform rolling rewraps at the KEK layer and re-encrypt DEKs without service interruption. In the very rare case of emergency manual rotation (operator-driven while a subset of nodes are being reprovisioned) there is a short window for affected hosts to re-establish key wrapping—this is mitigated by parallel key versions and failover routing; customers should not observe sustained 503s. We treat emergency rotation as a high-severity Ops event and notify impacted customers.

- On-prem BYOK: yes, Redwood supports customer-managed HSMs in private data centers (on-prem BYOK). Those keys can be marked non-exportable; Redwood operates against key APIs exposed by the customer's HSM. We never request exportable root material for on-prem BYOK.

Next steps:
- I've attached sample-hsm-log-lines.txt and kms_rotation_schedule.csv for your package. If Acme needs a signed attestation or a temporary secure artifact transfer (SFTP/secure drive), let us know the preferred channel and recipient.
- We can also do a 30-min call to walk auditors through the policy and logs — propose Wed 7/31 10:00am PT unless you prefer another time.

Thanks — happy to help close this out.
